blocks.tamil_translation: I am in need, I have the responsibility of looking after a wife and children, I will not come here again,' he said. I felt pity for him and let him go. In the morning the Prophet ﷺ asked again, “O Abu Hurairah, what did your captive do last night?” I said, “O Rasulullah, he complained of his great need and the poverty of his family, so I took pity on him and let him go.' The Prophet ﷺ said, Be careful. He is lying, he will come again. So again I waited for him, and the next night too (he came) and began scooping up grain with both his hands. I caught him and said, “I will certainly take you to Rasulullah ﷺ; this is the third and last time. You had said you would not come again, and you have come back again!' He said, “I will teach you some words (kalimahs) through which Allah will benefit you; let me go!” I said, “What are they?' He said, “When you go to sleep, recite Ayat al-Kursi; a guardian from Allah will be appointed for you. No Shaytan will come near you until morning.' In the morning the Prophet ﷺ asked, “What did your captive do last night? I said, “O Rasulullah, he said to me, “I will teach you some words through which Allah will benefit you,” so this time too I let him go.” Rasulullah ﷺ asked, “What are those words?' I said, he told me, “When you go to sleep, recite Ayat al-Kursi; Allah will appoint a guardian for you. No Shaytan will come near until morning.” The narrator of the hadith says,
